message.reasoning:
I am playing Monopoly as player p3.

I have $614 cash and six mortgaged properties. p1 has $1,196 and an orange monopoly with hotels on ST_JAMES, TENNESSEE, and NEW_YORK.

p2 is bankrupt. p4 has $247 and owns a purple and light blue monopoly with hotels, three unmortgaged railroads, and several mortgaged properties.

Unmortgaging Park Place would cost about $193. That would leave me with $421 cash. I still cannot build houses because Boardwalk is unmortgaged but Park Place remains mortgaged.

Building one house on each property would cost $400 and leave only $21 cash. That liquidity is too low to survive rent. I am now checking standard Monopoly hotel rent values for the light blue and purple monopolies.

I mapped the rent values for p4's monopolies. Mediterranean hotel is $250, Baltic hotel is $450, and the orange hotels are $950 to $1,000. Three railroads pay $100 each.

From GO, rolling a 3 lands on Baltic Avenue with a $450 hotel. Rolling a 6 or 8 lands on Oriental or Vermont with $550 hotels. Rolling a 9 lands on Connecticut with a $600 hotel. Rolling an 11 lands on St. Charles Place, which is mortgaged and costs nothing.

Rolling a 12 lands on my mortgaged Electric Company, which costs nothing. With $614 cash, I can survive every dangerous roll from GO. Unmortgaging Park Place would leave only $421, making the same rolls fatal. I am now considering whether to unmortgage the cheaper Electric Company instead.

Unmortgaging the remaining properties would cost too much for the rent they generate. Illinois, Atlantic, Marvin, and Pacific all lack monopolies or are owned by other players, so their base rents are too low to justify the cash burn. I am now considering mortgaging Boardwalk instead.

Boardwalk mortgage value is $200. That would raise cash to $814 but eliminate the only income source. The base rent of $50 is too small to justify the loss. I already survive the worst hotel with only $14 left. I am now weighing whether that extra cushion is worth the lost rent.

I will not mortgage Boardwalk preemptively. The cash can be raised later if needed, and the property would otherwise keep earning rent.

I can trade with p1 and p4. I am now looking for trades that could help me win.

I am in a difficult position. p1 has orange hotels. p4 has purple and light blue hotels plus three railroads. My dark blue monopoly is useless while both properties remain mortgaged.

I am using my mortgaged properties as blockers. Illinois blocks p1's reds, Pacific blocks p4's greens, and Atlantic plus Marvin block p4's yellows.

The game is late. p2 is dead. p1 and p4 will likely collide next.

p4 has only $247 cash. They just paid p1 $750 for Tennessee. They are extremely vulnerable. A hit on the orange hotels could bankrupt them unless they raise cash quickly.

p4 has already mortgaged St Charles, States, Virginia, Ventnor, Water Works, North Carolina, and Pennsylvania. They have no more mortgaged properties to use.

p4 could sell buildings on their hotels to raise cash, but they remain vulnerable to a hit on the orange hotels. p1 has $1,196 and sits on Kentucky, so they can survive most hits. My strategy is to survive until one opponent bankrupts the other. If p1 eliminates p4, they will inherit p4's properties and become unstoppable.

I am now evaluating which color groups I could complete through trades. The dark blue set is already mine, so no trade is needed there. The reds and yellows are harder to acquire because p1 and p4 would demand my Illinois or Atlantic and Marvin in return. The greens set is already complete.

I considered trading for p4's mortgaged North Carolina and Pennsylvania to complete the green monopoly. I also noted that both utilities are mortgaged, so acquiring Water Works would give me a second utility.

I then evaluated getting Ventnor from p4 to complete the yellow set. That would cost about $440 in unmortgage fees plus building expenses, leaving me with too little cash to build meaningfully this turn.

I am now considering selling a property to raise cash for building. The worst roll from GO is either Connecticut at $600 or a Chance card. I cannot afford to build houses and still survive that hit with only $614.

I will not build or unmortgage this turn. I am hoarding cash to survive until p1 and p4 damage each other.

I rejected trading Illinois to p1. That would give them a red monopoly with hotels, making them more dangerous.

I am now considering trading Pacific to p4 for cash or Ventnor.

Trading Pacific for p4 would let them build green hotels worth $1,275 to $1,400, which would be lethal. Giving them yellows would also be dangerous because yellow hotels pay $1,150 to $1,400.

I am now considering trading for Ventnor from p4. They might accept cash or another property in exchange because they are low on funds and recently paid $750.

I realized Ventnor is nearly worthless to p4 because they cannot unmortgage it without Atlantic and Marvin. Even if I could acquire it for free, the cost to unmortgage all three yellows would leave only about $174, which is still too little to build houses this turn. Any cash spent on Ventnor would shrink my survival margin further.

I am now calculating the exact cash needed to build houses on the dark blue set. Unmortgaging Park Place costs $193, and five houses on each property would cost $1,000 each. That leaves only $21 cash after building one house on Boardwalk. Even a hotel on Boardwalk would pay just $200, which is too little to survive a hit from p4's hotels. I will not build on the dark blues either.

I am now calculating the exact cost to build two hotels on the dark blue set. It would require $2,193 total, which is impossible with only $614 in cash.

I am now considering selling Illinois to p1 for a large sum of money. If p1 paid $800 to $1,000 for it, my cash would jump to $1,400 to $1,600. That would give me enough liquidity to unmortgage and build on the dark blues.

I calculated that even selling Illinois for all of p1's cash would leave only about $1,600 after unmortgaging Park Place. That is still short of the $2,000 needed for two hotels on the dark blue set. Four houses on both properties would cost $1,793, leaving just $17. Four houses on Boardwalk would pay $1,400 and on Park Place $1,100.

I realized that selling Illinois to p1 would leave them with no cash, so they could not build red hotels even though the red monopoly would double rent. They would rebuild quickly from their orange hotels. This trade is too risky, and p1 probably will not accept it.

I am now checking whether any Chance card could force a roll that costs more than $614 from GO. The worst possible hit is $600 for Connecticut, leaving only $14 of cash. I am reviewing the specific outcomes of a roll 7, such as landing on Reading Railroad at $100 or advancing to Boardwalk and Illinois, which are both mortgaged and worth nothing.

I am checking the board layout to see which railroad is nearest from the Chance space at position 7. The sequence shows Reading RR before Oriental, so the nearest one is likely Pennsylvania RR.

From the Chance space at position 7, the worst possible hits are $200 for the nearest railroad or Income Tax. The Electric Company is mortgaged and worth nothing. A poor tax card would cost only $15.

The worst possible Chance card is only $50 to p1, or $200 for the nearest railroad. Advancing to Boardwalk or Illinois would cost nothing since both are mortgaged. A trip to Reading Railroad costs $100.

The worst Community Chest card is only $150, so this roll is also survivable. I will not spend any cash this turn.

I considered offering Ventnor to p4 for a token price, but even a small payment would shrink my cash to $564 and leave me unable to survive the $600 Connecticut hotel. I cannot afford to spend any money this turn. The only safe play is to keep all $614 in hand and avoid any trade or building.

I will not trade. A lopsided offer would reveal desperation. I will end my turn.

message.reasoning:
I need to decide on a Monopoly action.

Cash dropped from $614 to $64 after paying $550 rent on VERMONT_AVENUE. All other properties except BOARDWALK are mortgaged.

p1 has a strong orange monopoly with hotels and $1,196 cash. p2 is bankrupt. p4 has $797 and many mortgaged properties. I can mortgage BOARDWALK for $200 to raise cash.

I'm reconsidering the early mortgage of BOARDWALK. With only $64 cash, I need to survive the next turn's rent payments. I'm mapping the board order to plan my next move from VERMONT_AVENUE.

Rolling from VERMONT_AVENUE lands on several properties. A 2 would hit CONNECTEDTOWN with a $600 hotel rent. A 7 would hit PENNSYLVANIA_RAILROAD for $100. A 8 would hit ST_JAMES with an orange hotel. Most other spaces are mortgaged and cost nothing.

St. James Place hotel rent is $950, which would wipe out my remaining $64 cash. I'm now mapping the exact sequence of spaces from Vermont Avenue to plan the safest next move.

Rolling a 2 on CONNECTEDTOWN would cost $600. Even with the $200 mortgage, I would still be $36 short. Rolling a 7 on PENNSYLVANIA_RAILROAD costs $100. That is manageable with the mortgage. I am now checking the remaining spaces.

Rolls 9, 11, and 12 are also fatal. Only rolls 3 through 7 are safe from immediate bankruptcy. The safest outcomes are landing on Jail, St. Charles Place, Electric Company, States Avenue, or Virginia Avenue.

I am weighing whether to mortgage Boardwalk now. Rolling a 7 on Pennsylvania Railroad costs $100, which is manageable with the mortgage. However, the previous strategy was to avoid early mortgages because the debt phase can handle it later and preserves the only rent-generating property.

I am now considering a trade. I could offer p1 my unmortgaged Illinois Avenue to complete their red monopoly, though they might build hotels afterward. I also need to check whether p4 owns yellows.

I now see that p4 only owns Ventnor among yellows, and I hold both Atlantic and Marvin. I also block p4 from greens with my unmortgaged Pacific. I have a dark blue monopoly of Park Place and Boardwalk, but Park Place is mortgaged and costs $193 to unmortgage. With only $64 cash, I cannot unmortgage it.

Mortgaging Boardwalk would leave only $71 after paying to unmortgage Park Place. That is too little to survive a roll on Connecticut or even Pennsylvania Railroad. Unmortgaging Park Place is therefore impossible.

I am now looking at trading. p1 wants Illinois Avenue to complete their red monopoly, but they still need to unmortgage Kentucky and Indiana before building.

Unmortgaging p1's red properties would cost $330 plus Illinois at $132. They could then build hotels and bankrupt me quickly. I would need to pay them heavily to unmortgage my dark blues and build houses, which costs $400. That trade is too expensive.

Trading away Boardwalk or Park Place would give p4 or p1 a complete color group they could develop, which is catastrophic. p4 already has light blue and purple hotels. I am now considering trading with p1 to hurt p4 instead.

I am now considering a passive survival strategy. With only $64 cash and no income properties unmortgaged except Boardwalk, I cannot afford to build or trade. The focus is simply staying alive until p1 and p4 bankrupt each other. p1 has just been sent to jail with $1,196 and orange hotels, while p4 has $797 and five hotels on light blues and purples. They will likely hit each other with their existing hotels. p1 may pay the $50 bail to leave or attempt to roll doubles.

I am now considering a trade to sell my mortgaged Electric Company for cash. It would not give away a monopoly, and p4 already owns Water Works, so the combined utility rent would be modest. I also confirmed that p1 would not pay for Illinois Avenue, since that would complete their red monopoly.

I will end the turn. I will not mortgage Boardwalk preemptively or trade away blockers and dark blues. The $64 cash is tight, but the debt phase can handle a mortgage if I land on Pennsylvania Railroad.

I realized that even with a $200 mortgage, landing on a hotel would still bankrupt me. I am now checking whether the trade schema allows trading properties without buildings, which would let me acquire cash while forcing opponents to sell their hotels.

The trade schema does not allow trading properties that have buildings on them, so I cannot acquire hotelled properties through a trade. I will end the turn without proposing any trades.
